```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(nbzinbPate)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.align = "center", out.width = "85%")

# Saved results of inst/benchmark/benchmark.R and simulation.R. Look in the
# installed package first, then in the source tree (when rendering from the
# repository before re-installing).
result_file <- function(name) {
  p <- system.file("benchmark", "results", name, package = "nbzinbPate")
  if (p == "") p <- file.path("..", "..", "inst", "benchmark", "results", name)
  p
}
bm  <- readRDS(result_file("benchmark.rds"))
sim <- readRDS(result_file("simulation.rds"))

# Formatting helpers
sci  <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1)
# "IRR (lower, upper)" or "OR (lower, upper)" from a 95% Wald interval
wald <- function(est, se) {
  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", exp(est), exp(est - qnorm(0.975) * se),
          exp(est + qnorm(0.975) * se))
}
```

# Introduction

::: {.callout-important}
## TODO (Brandon): Introduction

What the project asks you to cover (Sec 6.1, item 1):

* count data, and why the Poisson model is often too restrictive;
* **overdispersion** (variance > mean) and the NB2 model;
* **excess zeros** and the zero-inflated (two-process) model;
* the goals of the package: implement NB and ZINB estimation yourself
  (IRLS, Newton-Raphson, EM; no `optim()`), check it against
  `MASS::glm.nb()` and `pscl::zeroinfl()`, and apply it to NMES1988.
:::

# Methods

::: {.callout-important}
## TODO (Brandon): Methods prose

The equations below are the ones the code implements (Sec 2-3 of the
project description, plus the Hessian derivation in `R/zinb_hessian.R`).
Explain them in your own words: the models, the three algorithms, how
standard errors are computed, and the convergence criteria. Edit or cut
equations as you see fit.
:::

## Models

**NB2.** For counts $Y_i$ with covariates $x_i$ and offset $o_i$,
$$
P(Y_i = y) = \frac{\Gamma(y+\theta)}{\Gamma(\theta)\, y!}
  \left(\frac{\theta}{\theta+\mu_i}\right)^{\theta}
  \left(\frac{\mu_i}{\theta+\mu_i}\right)^{y},
\qquad \log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i,
$$
so that $E(Y_i)=\mu_i$ and $\mathrm{Var}(Y_i)=\mu_i+\mu_i^2/\theta$.

**ZINB.** With $\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma$,
$$
P(Y_i=0)=\pi_i+(1-\pi_i)f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta),\qquad
P(Y_i=y)=(1-\pi_i)f_{NB}(y;\mu_i,\theta),\ y\ge 1,
$$
$$
\ell(\beta,\gamma,\theta)=\sum_{y_i=0}\log\!\big[\pi_i+(1-\pi_i)f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta)\big]
+\sum_{y_i>0}\big[\log(1-\pi_i)+\log f_{NB}(y_i;\mu_i,\theta)\big].
$$

## NB: IRLS for $\beta$ alternated with Newton-Raphson for $\log\theta$

IRLS step, $\theta$ fixed:
$$
w_i = a_i\frac{\theta\mu_i}{\theta+\mu_i},\qquad
z_i = (\eta_i-o_i)+\frac{y_i-\mu_i}{\mu_i},\qquad
\beta^{(t+1)}=(X^\top WX)^{-1}X^\top Wz .
$$

Newton step on $\phi=\log\theta$, $\beta$ fixed:
$$
U(\theta)=\sum_i a_i\Big[\psi(y_i+\theta)-\psi(\theta)+\log\theta+1-\log(\theta+\mu_i)-\frac{y_i+\theta}{\theta+\mu_i}\Big],
$$
$$
H(\theta)=\sum_i a_i\Big[\psi'(y_i+\theta)-\psi'(\theta)+\frac1\theta-\frac{2}{\theta+\mu_i}+\frac{y_i+\theta}{(\theta+\mu_i)^2}\Big],
$$
$$
U_\phi=\theta U,\qquad H_\phi=\theta^2H+\theta U,\qquad \phi\leftarrow\phi-U_\phi/H_\phi .
$$

Standard errors: $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\beta)=(X^\top\hat WX)^{-1}$ and
$\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta)=\{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2}$.

## ZINB: EM with IRLS M-steps

E-step:
$$
\tau_i=\frac{\pi_i}{\pi_i+(1-\pi_i)f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta)}\ (y_i=0),\qquad \tau_i=0\ (y_i>0).
$$

M-step, zero part (fractional logistic IRLS):
$w_i=\pi_i(1-\pi_i)$, $z_i=z_i^\top\gamma+(\tau_i-\pi_i)/\{\pi_i(1-\pi_i)\}$.

M-step, count part: the NB fit above with prior weights $a_i=1-\tau_i$.

## Standard errors for ZINB: analytic Hessian

With $\eta^z_i=z_i^\top\gamma$, $\eta^c_i=x_i^\top\beta+o_i$,
$\ell^f_i=\log f_{NB}(y_i;\mu_i,\theta)$ and $a,b\in\{\eta^c,\phi\}$,
$$
\frac{\partial^2\ell_i}{\partial(\eta^z_i)^2}=\tau_i(1-\tau_i)-\pi_i(1-\pi_i),\quad
\frac{\partial^2\ell_i}{\partial\eta^z_i\,\partial a}=-\tau_i(1-\tau_i)\frac{\partial\ell^f_i}{\partial a},
$$
$$
\frac{\partial^2\ell_i}{\partial a\,\partial b}=(1-\tau_i)\frac{\partial^2\ell^f_i}{\partial a\,\partial b}
+\tau_i(1-\tau_i)\frac{\partial\ell^f_i}{\partial a}\frac{\partial\ell^f_i}{\partial b},
$$
and $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\beta,\hat\gamma,\log\hat\theta)=\{-H\}^{-1}$.

# The R package

::: {.callout-important}
## TODO (Brandon): Package design

Describe the design (Sec 6.1, item 3): the formula interfaces versus the
matrix-level engines (`nbreg_fit()` is reused as the ZINB count M-step),
the main functions, the S3 methods, the control functions, edge-case
handling (non-convergence, the Poisson limit, the no-zero-inflation
boundary), the tests, and installation.
:::

```{r install}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("brandonp8/nbzinbPate")
```

| Function | Purpose |
|:---|:---|
| `nbreg(formula, data, offset, control)` | NB2 regression: IRLS + Newton-Raphson for $\log\theta$ |
| `zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control)` | ZINB regression by EM; formula `y ~ x | z` |
| `nbreg_control()`, `zinbreg_control()` | tolerances, iteration limits, `trace` |
| S3 methods (both classes) | `print`, `summary`, `coef`, `vcov`, `logLik`, `AIC`/`BIC`, `fitted`, `residuals`, `nobs`, `predict` |

```{r usage}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(nbzinbPate)
data("NMES1988", package = "AER")
fit <- zinbreg(visits ~ hospital + health + chronic + gender + school +
                 insurance | hospital + chronic + gender + school + insurance,
               data = NMES1988)
summary(fit)
predict(fit, newdata = NMES1988[1:3, ], type = "zero")
```

# Benchmarking

::: {.callout-important}
## TODO (Brandon): Benchmarking prose

Summarize the agreement with `glm.nb()` / `zeroinfl()` on both data sets
against the Table 4 tolerances, and discuss the timings (why EM needs more
time than BFGS). Facts from the tables below: every quantity passes;
note whether our ZINB log-likelihood is higher than `zeroinfl()`'s
(`r if (bm$NMES1988$ZINB$loglik_higher) "it is, on NMES1988" else "it is not on NMES1988"`).
Full side-by-side estimates are in the Appendix.
:::

```{r bench-agreement}
agree <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("bioChemists", "NMES1988"), function(ds) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("NB", "ZINB"), function(m) {
    a <- bm[[ds]][[m]]$agreement
    data.frame(Data = ds, Model = m, Quantity = a$quantity,
               `Max abs. difference` = sci(a$max_abs_diff),
               Tolerance = sci(a$tolerance),
               Pass = ifelse(a$pass, "yes", "NO"), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(agree, booktabs = TRUE, align = "llllll",
             caption = paste("Maximum absolute difference between nbzinbPate",
                             "and MASS::glm.nb() (NB) or pscl::zeroinfl() (ZINB),",
                             "with the Table 4 tolerances."))
```

```{r bench-time}
timing <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("bioChemists", "NMES1988"), function(ds) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("NB", "ZINB"), function(m) {
    r <- bm[[ds]][[m]]
    data.frame(Data = ds, Model = m,
               `nbzinbPate (s)` = r$time[["ours"]],
               `Reference (s)` = r$time[["reference"]],
               Iterations = r$iterations, check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(timing, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2,
             caption = paste("Median computation time. Iterations: outer",
                             "IRLS/Newton iterations (NB) or EM iterations (ZINB)."))
```

# Simulation study

::: {.callout-important}
## TODO (Brandon): Simulation prose

Describe the design (below) and discuss the results: bias, mean SE versus
Monte Carlo SD, and coverage, taking the Monte Carlo error into account
(a coverage estimate from R = `r sim$design$R` replications has SE about
`r round(sim$diagnostics$coverage_mcse, 3)`).
Facts: `r sim$diagnostics$n_converged`/`r sim$design$R` fits converged,
`r sim$diagnostics$n_boundary` boundary cases,
`r sim$diagnostics$n_with_warnings` with warnings.
:::

Design: $R=`r sim$design$R`$ data sets of size $n=`r sim$design$n`$
(seed `r sim$design$seed`) with
$\log\mu_i=`r sim$design$beta[1]` + `r sim$design$beta[2]`\,x_{1i} `r sim$design$beta[3]`\,x_{2i}$,
$x_1\sim N(0,1)$, $x_2\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(0.5)$;
$\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i=`r sim$design$gamma[1]` + `r sim$design$gamma[2]`\,z_{1i}$, $z_1\sim N(0,1)$;
and $\theta=`r sim$design$theta`$.

```{r sim-table}
st <- sim$summary
names(st) <- c("Parameter", "True", "Mean est.", "Bias", "MC SD",
               "Mean SE", "SE / MC SD", "Coverage")
knitr::kable(st, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
             caption = paste("Simulation results: bias, Monte Carlo SD versus",
                             "mean estimated SE, and empirical coverage of",
                             "95% Wald intervals (theta on the log scale)."))
```

```{r sim-figure}
#| fig-cap: "Standardized errors (estimate - truth) / SE across the 100 replications. Under correct SEs these are approximately N(0, 1); dashed lines at +/-1.96."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 7
truth <- setNames(sim$summary$true, sim$summary$parameter)
zstd  <- sweep(sim$estimates, 2, truth) / sim$std_errors
op <- par(mar = c(8, 4, 1, 1))   # wide bottom margin for the rotated labels
boxplot(zstd, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.75, ylab = "(estimate - truth) / SE",
        col = "grey85")
abline(h = 0)
abline(h = c(-1.96, 1.96), lty = 2)
par(op)
```

# Data analysis: NMES1988

```{r nmes-data}
data("NMES1988", package = "AER")
d <- NMES1988
y <- d$visits
```

## Descriptive summary

```{r nmes-describe}
desc <- data.frame(
  n = length(y), Mean = mean(y), Variance = var(y),
  `Variance / mean` = var(y) / mean(y),
  `Observed zeros` = sum(y == 0),
  `Proportion zero` = mean(y == 0),
  `Poisson P(0) at the mean` = dpois(0, mean(y)),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(desc, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
             caption = "Physician office visits in NMES1988.")
```

## Models

```{r nmes-fit}
#| echo: true
f_count <- visits ~ hospital + health + chronic + gender + school + insurance
f_zinb  <- visits ~ hospital + health + chronic + gender + school + insurance |
  hospital + chronic + gender + school + insurance

m_pois <- glm(f_count, family = poisson, data = d)   # reference Poisson model
m_nb   <- nbreg(f_count, data = d)                     # our NB
m_zinb <- zinbreg(f_zinb, data = d)                    # our ZINB
```

```{r nmes-expected}
# Expected frequency of each count k under each fitted model:
# sum over observations of the fitted P(Y_i = k).
K <- 0:30
exp_pois <- sapply(K, function(k) sum(dpois(k, fitted(m_pois))))
exp_nb   <- sapply(K, function(k) sum(dnbinom(k, size = m_nb$theta,
                                              mu = fitted(m_nb))))
pi_hat <- predict(m_zinb, type = "zero")
mu_hat <- predict(m_zinb, type = "count")
exp_zinb <- sapply(K, function(k) {
  sum((k == 0) * pi_hat +
        (1 - pi_hat) * dnbinom(k, size = m_zinb$theta, mu = mu_hat))
})
obs <- sapply(K, function(k) sum(y == k))
```

```{r nmes-freq-figure}
#| fig-cap: "Observed frequencies of office visits (bars) and frequencies expected under the fitted Poisson, NB and ZINB models, for 0-20 visits."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 7
show <- K <= 20
op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
bp <- barplot(obs[show], names.arg = K[show], col = "grey85", border = "grey50",
              ylim = c(0, max(obs, exp_pois) * 1.05),
              xlab = "Number of physician office visits", ylab = "Frequency")
lines(bp, exp_pois[show], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "firebrick")
lines(bp, exp_nb[show],   type = "b", pch = 17, col = "steelblue")
lines(bp, exp_zinb[show], type = "b", pch = 15, col = "darkgreen")
legend("topright", c("Observed", "Poisson", "NB", "ZINB"),
       pch = c(22, 19, 17, 15), pt.bg = c("grey85", NA, NA, NA),
       col = c("grey50", "firebrick", "steelblue", "darkgreen"), bty = "n")
par(op)
```

## Model comparison

```{r nmes-compare}
cmp <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Poisson", "NB", "ZINB"),
  df = c(attr(logLik(m_pois), "df"), attr(logLik(m_nb), "df"),
         attr(logLik(m_zinb), "df")),
  logLik = c(logLik(m_pois), logLik(m_nb), logLik(m_zinb)),
  AIC = c(AIC(m_pois), AIC(m_nb), AIC(m_zinb)),
  BIC = c(BIC(m_pois), BIC(m_nb), BIC(m_zinb)),
  `Expected zeros` = c(exp_pois[1], exp_nb[1], exp_zinb[1]),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cmp, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 1,
             caption = sprintf(paste("Model comparison for NMES1988",
                                     "(observed zeros = %d)."), obs[1]))
```

## Interpretation: incidence rate ratios and odds ratios

```{r nmes-irr}
s_nb <- summary(m_nb)$coefficients
s_zc <- summary(m_zinb)$coefficients$count
keep_nb <- rownames(s_nb) != "(Intercept)"
keep_zc <- !(rownames(s_zc) %in% c("(Intercept)", "Log(theta)"))
irr <- data.frame(
  Covariate = rownames(s_nb)[keep_nb],
  `NB IRR (95% CI)` = wald(s_nb[keep_nb, 1], s_nb[keep_nb, 2]),
  `ZINB count IRR (95% CI)` = wald(s_zc[keep_zc, 1], s_zc[keep_zc, 2]),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(irr, booktabs = TRUE, row.names = FALSE, align = "lcc",
             caption = "Count part: incidence rate ratios with 95% Wald intervals.")
```

```{r nmes-or}
s_zz <- summary(m_zinb)$coefficients$zero
keep_zz <- rownames(s_zz) != "(Intercept)"
or <- data.frame(
  Covariate = rownames(s_zz)[keep_zz],
  `OR (95% CI)` = wald(s_zz[keep_zz, 1], s_zz[keep_zz, 2]),
  `p-value` = format.pval(s_zz[keep_zz, 4], digits = 2, eps = 1e-4),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(or, booktabs = TRUE, row.names = FALSE, align = "lcc",
             caption = paste("ZINB zero part: odds ratios of being a",
                             "structural zero (never visiting), with 95% Wald",
                             "intervals."))
```

# AI-use statement

::: {.callout-important}
## TODO (Brandon): AI-use statement (in your own words)

Sec 6.1, item 8: how you used Claude Code, what you asked it to do, what
you verified yourself, and at least one example where you had to correct
or reject its output. Episodes from the development history (see the git
log) that you may draw on:

* **IRLS stopping rule (step 2):** the first version stopped on the
  log-likelihood change and left the score at 0.011 (beta accurate only to
  ~1e-6); changed to the largest change in beta.
* **Poisson-limit test (step 4):** the test used `rpois()` data that were
  overdispersed by chance, so theta-hat = 88 was correct and the expected
  warning was wrong; replaced with underdispersed data.
* **No-zero-inflation boundary (step 6):** with an intercept-only zero
  model, gamma -> -Inf; EM ran 1000 iterations; added boundary detection.
* **glm.nb SE(theta) explanation:** an initial explanation of the 1e-6
  difference was imprecise and was corrected after reading the MASS source.
* **Step-halving rounding bug (CI on macOS):** exact comparison of
  log-likelihoods in the step-halving safeguard caused false convergence
  on macOS only; fixed with a rounding-aware comparison and regression
  tests that inject rounding noise.
* **README:** an over-strong agreement claim was corrected.
:::

# Appendix: side-by-side benchmark estimates {.appendix}

```{r appendix-tables}
#| results: asis
for (ds in c("bioChemists", "NMES1988")) {
  for (m in c("NB", "ZINB")) {
    tab <- bm[[ds]][[m]]$table
    tab$abs_diff <- sci(tab$abs_diff)
    names(tab) <- c("Quantity", "Parameter", "nbzinbPate", "Reference",
                    "Abs. difference")
    ref_name <- if (m == "NB") "MASS::glm.nb()" else "pscl::zeroinfl()"
    print(knitr::kable(tab, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,
                       caption = sprintf("%s, %s: nbzinbPate vs %s.",
                                         ds, m, ref_name)))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```
